messages.content: How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?

function.name: calculate_projectile_range
function.description: Calculate the range of a projectile launched at an angle with initial velocity, using the kinematic equation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity at which projectile is launched. This is a float type value.

angle.description: The angle at which projectile is launched. This should be in degrees. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time in seconds after which the range is to be calculated. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?" They want to compute distance traveled given initial velocity v, launch angle theta, and time t. This is essentially projectile motion horizontal displacement: x = v * cos(theta) * t. But they mention "calculate_projectile_range" function. That function calculates range (horizontal distance) given initial velocity, angle, and optional time. It returns something. We need to call the function with arguments: initial_velocity: v, angle: theta, time: t. Then we output the result.

We need to use the function. So we call functions.calculate_projectile_range with those parameters. The function signature: initial_velocity: number, angle: number, time?: number default 0.5. So we pass all three. Then we get the result. We'll respond with the result. Probably the function returns the horizontal distance. So we just call it.
